# PROCESS — round 1, sibling cand_1a (siblings cand_1a / cand_1b / cand_1c share this diagnosis)

## Ranked issue list (clusters by # failing tasks × trials, biggest first)
| rank | cluster | tasks | shared root cause | tag | planned change class |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | "N cell(s) hold a number LOWER than expected" | 374-9 (t0,t1,t2), 53161 (t2) | `openpyxl.load_workbook(p)` WITHOUT `data_only=True` returns a formula cell as its formula STRING; the agent's own `isinstance(v,(int,float))` guard then silently drops it. No error, totals simply low. | KNOWLEDGE | add the missing fact + worked example (`prompt.md`) / force a typed print in round 1 (`task_template.md`) |
| 2 | verification is a PRINT, never a COMPARISON | all 9 failing trials; 0 of 12 passing traces compare either | the round-3 instruction said "re-open output_path and print the values you wrote", so the agent reads its own numbers back and declares success. 32468 t2 printed a list literally ending in `None` and shipped it; 32468 t1/t2 then re-sent byte-identical code 3× | BEHAVIORAL (structure) | replace print-back with an ordered check-by-comparison step (recompute one cell by a second route, count vs TARGET SIZE, row count before/after, any total the instruction names) |
| 3 | invented filler written into cells the answer leaves alone | 55457 t0/t2 (5 cells), 32468 t2 (`results.append(None)`) | `else: results.append(0)` pads the inactive part of the range; scorer reports "written past where the answer ends" + "CHANGED although the expected value is the cell's own original input", and the all-`0` column also flips the dtype to int | CONTRACT | state the contract, WITH a carve-out for instruction-directed blanking |
| 4 | DataFrame-index vs Excel-row off-by-one | 40467 t2, 32468 t2 | `pd.read_excel(p)` consumes Excel row 1 as the header; pairing it with `to_excel(..., header=False)` (40467 t2) or with openpyxl 1-based writes (32468 t2 `range(4,35)` → `row=5+idx`) shifts every answer one row. 40467 t0/t1 PASS with the consistent `header=None`/`header=False` pairing — a clean A/B | KNOWLEDGE | state the three offsets and the read/write pairing rule |
| 5 | extent derived from an assumption, not the data | 53161 t0 (`range(6,31)` = F..AD, missing AE → exactly the 8 empty cells), 347-49 (blank-run scan stops at the first non-blank row → deletes 10 rows where gold deletes 72), 53161 t2 (hardcoded table rows point at the wrong block → all zeros) | Python's exclusive upper bound + row numbers assumed rather than searched for | KNOWLEDGE + structure | count-vs-TARGET-SIZE check; search for the marker and print where it was found |
| 6 | (not addressable) semantic guesses | 32468 t0/t1 (12- vs 13-month window), 55457 all | 32468's window is a genuine judgement call, reachable only via the ~39M anchor the instruction names; 55457's `instruction` field is literally blank (`' '`), so its value semantics are unknowable — only its filler/type damage is addressable | — | deliberately not chased with prose |

No ENVIRONMENT fault found: all 30 rollouts ran, produced an output file, and were scored. `errored_trials: 0` on every task. The failures are capability failures.

## Changes made this round (three siblings, same clusters, DIFFERENT surface/form — so the round learns which form the reader responds to)
| sibling | surface | edit class | what & why it generalizes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| cand_1a | `prompt.md` only | add-a-sourced-rule + worked example (classes 4 & 5 of the system-prompt skill) | four sections: the `data_only=True` fact with a two-handle worked example; the no-filler contract with its carve-out; the DataFrame/Excel offset table; derive-extents-from-data. All are general facts about openpyxl/pandas/Excel, no task id or value |
| cand_1b | `task_template.md` only | restructure + tighten the output contract (classes 6 & 8), including a DELETION | the round list becomes an ordered procedure where each step is a precondition of the next; round 1 must print source cells with their types before any arithmetic; round 3 is check-by-comparison. Deleted "Reply without a code block when you are satisfied the saved file is correct" and the print-back wording — text the traces show is actively harmful |
| cand_1c | both | composition | 1a's knowledge in `prompt.md`, a shorter ordered procedure in `task_template.md` that invokes the checks rather than restating the facts |

## Verify-the-fix (one line per change)
- **data_only (cluster 1):** trace 374-9 t0 `wb = openpyxl.load_workbook(file_path)` then `if isinstance(val,(int,float)): sum_a += val`. Column H is labelled 'A' in row 6 and holds `'=SUM(A7:G7)'` for rows 7–16, so 10 rows of column B lost their largest term. VERIFIED END-TO-END: replaying that same final code with `data_only=True` added and nothing else changed makes all 32 cells match gold, including the float type on B10 (`9318.93` vs the written int `2109`) — 0/3 becomes 3/3.
- **check-by-comparison (cluster 2):** trace 374-9 t1 verification prints `Row 10: Col B = 2109, Col C = 3160.93` — B (3 source columns) smaller than C (2) — and the agent replies "The verification output confirms that values have been calculated and written... No further changes are needed." A recompute-by-a-second-route check yields 3834386 for B7 against the written 1086469, a 3.5× disagreement on the first asserted cell. Made a PRECONDITION of finishing, not advice: "reply without a code block once a comparison in round 3 has AGREED".
- **no filler (cluster 3):** trace 55457 t0 `else: results.append(0)` → the scorer's "5 cell(s) hold a value where the expected output has none" + "5 cell(s) were CHANGED although the expected value is the cell's own original input". Trial t1 is the A/B: it dropped that branch (`else: pass`) and lost all five of those violations at no cost in correct values.
- **row offset (cluster 4):** trace 40467 t2 `pd.read_excel(file_path)` + `to_excel(..., header=False)` printed 9 values starting `'From 08-Jan to 12-Jan'`, where passing t0/t1 print 10 starting `'From 01-Jan to 05-Jan'` — exactly the scorer's "value in 9 of them / 1 cell empty / 9 of the right type but wrong". The stated pairing rule reproduces t0/t1's behaviour.
- **extent (cluster 5):** trace 53161 t0 `for c in range(6, 31): # Col F to AE` — the comment says AE, the range ends at AD. Its other 200 cells were already correct, so column AE is the entire gap between 0/3 and passing. The count-vs-TARGET-SIZE print surfaces 25 vs 26 immediately.

## Blast radius (checked against all 12 passing traces, per edit)
- `data_only=True` — **BOUNDED.** 52216 t1/t2 already call `load_workbook(file_path, data_only=True)`. 47484, 160-6, 418-29 read through pandas, which already returns cached values, so the rule is a no-op. 52216 t0 reads without the flag and does see `=_xlfn.IFNA(...)` in C15, but never uses that value; adding the flag was verified to produce byte-identical output.
- no-filler contract — **BOUNDED, because of the carve-out.** 47484 and 52216 write only asked-for cells already. 418-29's gold BLANKS 4 cells inside answer_position and 160-6's gold leaves rows 9–11 blank, so the rule is phrased to forbid INVENTED padding only and explicitly to permit instruction-directed blanking and row-shift blanks.
- offset / extent / no-repeat rules — **BOUNDED.** Statements of fact about the libraries, consistent with what every passing trace already does; 40467 t0/t1's passing pairing is the rule's own worked example.
- ordered procedure (1b/1c) — **BOUNDED but the largest surface.** It does not forbid any mechanism. The replayed block is the last one that CHANGED the graded file (`adapter.py:1305-1308`), so an extra pure-check round is correctly not replayed — 52216 t2 already demonstrates this (replayed block = msg 8, last block = msg 10). Risk noted: 47484 and 52216 already consume all 5 rounds, so an added inspect round displaces a solve round.

## Three rules I diagnosed as UNSAFE and deliberately did NOT ship
This is the round's main negative finding, and it cost nothing to learn. Half this suite is row-deletion / row-shift work, not fill-a-column work, so each of these plausible rules regresses a currently-passing task:
1. *"Always edit in place with openpyxl; never rebuild with `df.to_excel`."* — 160-6's passing mechanism IS `dropna(how='all')` + `to_excel` (the row shift is the answer); it would also force 47484 and 418-29 t0/t1 off their winning approach. 8 of 12 passing traces.
2. *"Leave every cell outside answer_position identical; never blank a cell inside it."* — FALSE on this benchmark: 160-6's own gold changes 30 cells OUTSIDE answer_position, 418-29's gold blanks 4 INSIDE it, 347-49's gold blanks 237. Confirmed from the adapter that grading reads ONLY cells inside answer_position (`adapter.py:1712`), so the outside-range claim is not even a contract the scorer holds.
3. *"Diff input vs output and fix any outside-range difference."* — would order 160-6 to undo its correct row shift, converting 3/3 into ~0.

## Process & features used
- Three read-only diagnoser subagents in parallel (one per cluster group, one dedicated to establishing the passing-task blast radius). Zero rollouts spent on diagnosis. Their findings were independently re-checked against the real fixture workbooks, which is how the `data_only=True` fix and the 347-49 10-vs-72-row count were confirmed rather than merely hypothesised.
- Prior iterations read: none exist — this is round 1 (LEDGER holds the baseline row only, `prior_iterations/` empty, `rejected.jsonl` absent).
- Screen ladder deliberately skipped (`--skip-screen-ladder`): on a 10-task val the tier-1 floor puts `savings.breakeven_kill_rate` out of reach, so full val is the cheaper honest path — SKILL.md's own guidance.

## Good things to PRESERVE
- The three unsafe rules above: do not re-derive them. The generalisation "this suite is only fill-a-column tasks" is false and is the trap.
- Round 1's measured resolution: two BYTE-IDENTICAL controls differed by **0.1333** on full val at 3 trials, and the stored seed vs a fresh control differed by 0.1. No effect smaller than ~0.13 is resolvable at this n on this 10-task split. Any future round reporting a Δ of 0.05–0.10 as a win is reading noise.

## Deliberately skipped
- 55457's value semantics (`instruction` is literally a blank string — unknowable; only its filler/type damage was addressed).
- 32468's 12- vs 13-month window (a semantic judgement; encoding "use 13" would be fitting one task's answer, not a general rule).
